today.question_title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array II
hints_cache: This is a classic 'searching' problem where the data is mostly sorted. Since you want to find a specific value faster than looking at every single element, think about how you can repeatedly cut your search area in half.

In a normal binary search, you compare the middle to a target. Here, try comparing the middle element to the rightmost element of your current window to decide which half is 'normal' and which half is 'rotated.'

If the middle element is strictly less than the right element, the right side is sorted, so the minimum must be at or to the left of the middle. If the middle is strictly greater, the 'drop-off' (and the minimum) must be to the right.

The 'Hard' part is when the middle and right elements are exactly the same. When this happens, you can't be sure which side to discard, but you know for a fact that the rightmost element is redundant because the middle element has the same value.

To handle duplicates, simply shrink your search window by moving the right boundary inward by one step whenever the middle and right elements are equal. This preserves the minimum while slowly clearing the ambiguity until you can resume your jump-searches.
